turns.q:
Your response was: "The summary layout is clear. The "Continue Shopping" button size is distracting. The legal text at bottom is small."

We want to understand what you meant by "The "Continue Shopping" button size is distracting", so let's go a bit deeper. Which of these best captures what you were pointing at?

A) The "Continue Shopping" button appears as a large full-width element beneath Payment Details, making it more prominent than the checkout action below it.

B) The "Continue Shopping" button takes up a tall horizontal block in the lower part of the page, creating too much visual weight in the layout.

C) The "Continue Shopping" button is positioned above "Place Order," so its large size disrupts the expected priority of the checkout actions.

D) None of the above — but only if A, B, and C genuinely miss what you meant (you must still name the specific element you were referring to)

Select A, B, C, or D to continue.
What were you checking or verifying when the large “Continue Shopping” button appeared above “Place Order”?
turns.a: Whether checkout was intentionally blocked. The grey “Place Order” reads disabled. The black button above it reads as the available command, which is wrong for checkout.

turns.q: What part of the order-summary layout or action area were you looking at when the oversized “Continue Shopping” button first felt out of place?
turns.a: The stack under Payment Details. Fields end, then the black full-width “Continue Shopping” appears before the grey “Place Order.” That sequence makes the wrong action look operationally primary.

turns.q: What is the core purpose the Payment Details area and final action section need to serve, given that “Continue Shopping” currently appears more prominent than “Place Order”?
turns.a: Capture payment, then confirm purchase. The final action should be unambiguous: complete the order. “Continue Shopping” should not compete with that command.

turns.q: What would need to change in the placement, size, or styling of “Continue Shopping” and “Place Order” so the checkout priority is immediately clear?
turns.a: Move “Place Order” directly under Payment Details as the full-width black primary button. Put “Continue Shopping” below it as a text link or smaller outline button. If “Place Order” is disabled, keep it in that position and state why: “Enter payment details to place order.”
